what: The measurement behind `maintenance_every`'s default (docs/M8-MAINTENANCE.md, issue #12). Three candidates ran the soak workload (windows of 16 writes, previous window tainted away — retract-as-you-go) against the release binary for 280 s each on the same host, measuring throughput, the worst single-write stall (a maintenance pass lands on the write path's tail), and the storage footprint the policy is meant to bound.
harness: same-host release mutinyd, one tenant, HTTP door driven by curl (per-write timing includes client overhead of ~30-50 ms, identical across candidates); 2026-08-21, Apple Silicon macOS (Darwin 24.6.0)
reading: Throughput is equal within noise (±3%). The worst-stall column is a single maximum and is noise-dominated (it is not monotone in the candidate), so it distinguishes nothing here beyond 'sub-second in all cases'. The real difference is exactly what the policy promises: the storage residue between passes scales with N (manifest files at end: 1 / 33 / 17 ≈ commits since the last pass), and every candidate holds storage three orders of magnitude under the unbounded failure mode this fixes (~75 MB and growing at the same workload length, see #12).

choice.why: With throughput and stalls indistinguishable at this workload, 64 keeps the residue bound tight (at most 64 commits of un-collapsed history) without paying the pass's fixed cost (engine checkpoint + snapshot) four times as often as 16 would for no measured benefit. Config overrides per tenant; 0 disables (dev only — the nightly soak gates the default).
